div.head: Rect 12, 12.1
div.ab: [12] Be oxanhyrde. Oxanhyrde mot læswian II oxan oððe ma mid hlafordes heorde on gemænre læse be his ealdormannes gewitnesse; earnian mid ðam scos ⁊ glofa him sylfum. [12.1] ⁊ his metecu mot gan mid hlafordes oxan.

Bubulco licet adherbare duos boues–et alicubi plus–cum grege domini in communibus pascuis, per testimonium tamen aldremanni sui; deseruiat per id calceos et cirothecas sibi. [12.1] Et eius metecu (id est uictus sui uaccam) licet ire cum bobus domini.

Be oxan | hyrde Oxanhyrde mot læswian .ii. oxan oððe ma mid hlafordes heorde on gemænre læse be his ealdormannes gewitnesse . ear|nian mid ðam scos 7 glofa him sylfum .7 his metecu mot gan mid hlafordes oxan.

Be oxanhyrde Oxanhyrde mot læswian II oxan oððe ma mid hlafordes heorde on gemænre læse be his ealdormannes gewitnesse; earnian mid ðam scos and glofa him sylfum. [12.1] And his metecu mot gan mid hlafordes oxan.

Vom Ochsenhirten. Der Ochsenhirt darf 2 [eigene] Ochsen oder mehr mit der herrschaftlichen Herde auf gemeiner Weide weiden unter Vorwissen seines Vorgesetzten [und] durch dies [Hüten] sich Schuhe und Handschuhe verdienen. [12.1] Und seine Nährkuh darf mit des Herrn Ochsen [weiden] gehen.

[12] Of the oxherd. The oxherd may pasture 2 [of his own] oxen or more with the lord's herd on common pasture with the knowledge of his superior, [and] by this [herding] earn himself shoes and gloves. [12.1] And his food-cow may go [to pasture] with the lord's oxen.

Concerning the oxherd The oxherd may graze two oxen or more with the lord’s herd on the common pasture with the knowledge of his overseer, [and he may] earn with them shoes and gloves for himself. And his food-cow may go with the lord’s oxen.

Regarding the Oxherd The oxherd may graze two oxen or more with the lord’s herd in the common pasture with his overseer’s knowledge; he may earn shoes and gloves for himself with them. [12.1] And the cow he intends for food may go with the lord’s oxen.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 12–12.1. The Quadripartitus understands ‘earnie’; but perhaps ‘⁊’ should be supplied before it, the infinitive depending on ‘mot’. Liebermann compares Rect 17, 10, 8 and 13.1.
This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (12, 12.1), each marked with its number.

note.seg: earnie versteht Quadr.; vielleicht aber ist ⁊ davor zu ergänzen, und hängt der Infinitiv von mot ab
Quadr. understands earnie; but perhaps ⁊ should be supplied before it, and the infinitive depends on mot
Unfrei laut der Ausstattung mit einer Nährkuh und laut IV Eg 9. So Andrews 213 gegen Leo. Wär er ein Dorfbauer, so stände seinem Rind die Gemeinweide deshalb frei

Unfree, to judge from his being provided with a cow for his keep, and from IV Eg 9. So Andrews 213, against Leo. Were he a village peasant, the common pasture would by that very fact be open to his cattle

Verf. braucht gewitnesse, das sehr oft ‘Aufsicht’ bed., für ‘Bewilligung’. Die Domäne gewährleistet zugleich den ehrlichen Besitz dieser Rinder. Das Vieh muss nämlich, gegen Diebstahlsverdacht, öffentlich bekannt sein; IV Eg 8

The author uses gewitnesse, which very often means ‘supervision’, for ‘permission’. At the same time the demesne vouches for the honest possession of these cattle. For the livestock must be publicly known, as a safeguard against suspicion of theft; IV Eg 8
Nicht verstanden ist, auch 17, der staatliche Graf, sondern entweder der Herr (Andrews Manor 144) oder wahrscheinlicher der Vogt
What is meant, here as in 17, is not the public reeve, but either the lord (Andrews Manor 144) or, more probably, the bailiff
